ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a heptagonal ring-shaped arrangement divided from the center into 7 sector positions. The heart shape is in a position on the upper-left side, and the arrow is in another position on the lower-right side; the two are initially not in the same cell. Then reason: Number the 7 positions modulo 7. In each round, the arrow moves 3 cells clockwise; the heart shape moves 4 cells counterclockwise, which is moving -4 cells modulo 7. Because -4 ≡ 3 (mod 7), the net movement of the heart shape each round is equivalent to moving 3 cells clockwise. Thus after each round, the heart shape and the arrow both move the same 3 cells relative to the whole, and the interval between them always remains unchanged. Since at the beginning they are not in the same position, they will also never land in the same position afterward.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the figure is a 7-place circular/heptagonal arrangement divided into seven wedge-shaped regions, with the heart and the arrow starting in two different regions. From the text, one routine moves the arrow 3 places clockwise and the heart 4 places anticlockwise. Model the seven places modulo 7. Moving 4 anticlockwise is equivalent to moving 3 clockwise, since -4 ≡ 3 mod 7. Therefore, after every routine, both objects have shifted by the same net amount around the 7-place cycle, so their initial separation never changes. Because they do not start in the same place, they will never land in the same place.
